claims.claim: Year 1 pupils distinguish an object from the material it is made of, name wood, plastic, glass and metal, and describe simple properties, which this lesson teaches.

sources.title: National curriculum in England: science programmes of study (Year 1 plants, everyday materials; Year 2 living things)

notes: safety: the teaching text says metal 'can be put on the fire' (金屬很硬，可以放在火上) to a 5-year-old with no warning that metal on a fire gets very hot and burns, and no pointer that only a trusted adult uses the stove or fire. This is dangerous to imitate. Teach the property as 'metal does not burn or melt easily; pots are metal; hot pots are for grown-ups to handle'.
Example '本子是紙做的': '本子' is the Mainland word; in Traditional-Chinese (Taiwan/HK) children's books it is '筆記本' or '簿子'. Correct: '筆記本是紙做的'.
